beats.headline: Benjamin, on a stick
beats.text: For the record: about fifteen dwarven kids in patched clothes play in the street beside the elves' temple. One of the older ones chases the rest with a small salamander tied to a stick and jabs it at a robed elf; the lizard spits a single spark. Left in the street, it tries to drag itself away, and Mongo swallows it whole with half the stick. It comes back up, dead, in the middle of a standoff. "Benjamin?" asks the young dwarf. Ricky Joe. Level 2. Juvenile Fathom Dwarf.

beats.headline: He punches the raptor
beats.text: His mother, Eunice, level-30 fathom dwarf and enormously pregnant, has been frozen solid by an Icer, and the swordsmen guards raise their blades over her. Crawler Carl punches a guard. At the same moment Ricky Joe punches Mongo in the face: "You killed my best friend!" On the second swing his arm is no longer there. Mongo has bitten it off below the elbow and swallowed it, along with Benjamin, for the second time. Crawler Donut's "Mongo, hold!" saves his life. Carl tucks the bleeding boy under his arm like a football.

beats.headline: Give me my arm back
beats.text: Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper takes the crawlers and the boy to a rooftop across the street as the boom jug lands below and crisps the remaining eight elves. Crawler Carl shoves a health potion into the squealing boy's mouth. The blood stops, and his health returns to green. His arm does not grow back. He moves to hit the dinosaur again with his left, and Carl holds him back. "Give it back! Give me my arm back!"

beats.headline: Benjamin was in training
beats.text: He sits cross-legged on the roof, clutching his severed limb and Benjamin's twice-eaten corpse. He screamed bloody murder on learning the arm could not be reattached, and Crawler Donut talked him down. Told that tying a lizard to a stick is not cool: at least he did not eat him, and Benjamin liked it. Fathom dwarves strap them to their hats when they go into mines. He was in training. The boy's own home, attached to the temple, has burned to the ground.

beats.headline: The skyfowl lady
beats.text: Asked about the temple: the elves were always weird. One cried for his mama every morning, through the walls. His brother Bubba Lane saw something fly from the roof a couple of nights ago, probably just that skyfowl lady. She visits a lot, just before dark, and leaves with a bunch of other ladies, elves and dwarves and humans, dressed like they are going to the Desperado. Where she takes them he does not know. They are not allowed past the street.

beats.headline: In charge of the left leg
beats.text: Crawler Carl carries the protesting boy down the rope under his arm and drops him the last ten feet. He belly-flops, loses his grip on the arm and the salamander, and wails. His health has barely blipped. "Walk it off, kid." A scream from the building next door: "That's me mom." She is in labor again, and she is going to be really mad if he misses it. He is in charge of holding her left leg. "Bye, Princess Donut! Bye Mongo!"

beats.headline: Whether the baby came
beats.text: On the stairs down, Crawler Carl runs through everyone they met on this floor. Among them, little Ricky Joe, the one-armed child dwarf, whose word that a female skyfowl was visiting the city elves had first made Carl suspect Miss Quill. He wonders whether the boy's mom ever had her baby.
